lead_headline: Arvada Council Unanimously Adopts First Climate & Sustainability Action Plan

type_specific.meeting_summary: The Arvada City Council held its July 7, 2026 business meeting, taking several significant votes including unanimous adoption of the city's first Climate and Sustainability Action Plan (CASP) and advancing four ordinances to first reading. The council also heard public comment on a potential motion to reconsider the previously denied Avalon Bay conditional use permit at Welby Gardens, but none of the three eligible council members made such a motion, leaving the April 21 denial in place. The meeting also included a public hearing on rezoning requests for three undeveloped Candelas parcels from commercial/industrial PUD to residential and commercial designations.

tonight_at_a_glance.synopsis: Council voted 7–0 to adopt Arvada's inaugural Climate and Sustainability Action Plan and declined to reopen the denied Avalon Bay apartment project. A public hearing on Candelas parcels 12, 15, and 16 rezoning was also opened.
highlights: Climate and Sustainability Action Plan adopted unanimously (7–0)
No motion made to reconsider denied Avalon Bay/Welby Gardens conditional use permit — denial stands
Four ordinances on Comcast franchise renewal and Revival Industrial annexation/rezoning referred to first reading (7–0)
Three consent agenda resolutions covering construction, CDOT signal upgrades, and Lakeside fleet maintenance approved (7–0)
Public hearing opened on Candelas parcels 12, 15, and 16 rezoning from PUD to residential and commercial designations

presentations.topic: Climate and Sustainability Action Plan (CASP) Presentation
presentations.presenter_role: Senior Sustainability Coordinator, City of Arvada
prose_paragraphs: Senior Sustainability Coordinator Stephen Russell presented the final 2026 Climate and Sustainability Action Plan for council adoption. He summarized the science of human-caused climate change, noted that Arvada has already achieved a 17% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions since 2015 (largely due to Xcel Energy's grid transition), and outlined conservative goals for reducing both city government and communitywide emissions. Russell noted the plan includes approximately 150 tracking metrics, commits to annual action plans and reporting, and involved over 450 individual public recommendations during a formal comment period. He emphasized the plan contains no mandates and is designed as a guiding framework to be implemented across city departments.

presenter_quotes.text: While humanity may have missed the train on preventing climate change outright, we still have the power to improve our situation by first reducing our greenhouse gas emissions urgently and second by building out resilient systems to help keep future generations safe and prosperous in a GHG altered climate.

public_hearings.what_is_being_heard: Council was asked to consider whether one of three eligible members would make a motion to reconsider the April 21, 2026 decision denying CB26-008, a conditional use permit for Avalon Bay Communities' proposed apartment project known as Welby Gardens at approximately 17201 West 64th Avenue. The original vote was a 3–3 tie (failing under the city charter's requirement of four votes to pass). Avalon Bay twice requested reconsideration under City Council Rule of Procedure 4L. Council Member Davis was recused. No vote on the merits of the project was taken; the only question was whether Mayor Simpson, Council Member Leon, or Council Member Feifer would make a motion to reopen the matter.

public_hearings.what_is_being_heard: Council opened a public hearing on six related land use actions for Candelas Parcels 12, 15, and 16, located at the northeast corner of Highway 72 and Highway 93. The applicant requests three comprehensive plan amendments (changing parcels from Neighborhood Community Commercial to High Density Residential, Medium Density Residential, and Suburban Residential designations respectively) and three corresponding rezonings from PUD to R24, R13, R6, and CG. The parcels have been designated for commercial/industrial use under the existing PUD but the applicant argues market conditions no longer support that development. The Planning Commission approved the comprehensive plan amendments and recommended approval of the rezonings at its February 4, 2026 meeting. The concept plan indicates up to approximately 780 residential units across the parcels.

meeting_summary: The Arvada City Council held its July 7, 2026 business meeting, taking several significant votes including unanimous adoption of the city's first Climate and Sustainability Action Plan (CASP) and advancing four ordinances to first reading. The council also heard public comment on a potential motion to reconsider the previously denied Avalon Bay conditional use permit at Welby Gardens, but none of the three eligible council members made such a motion, leaving the April 21 denial in place. The meeting also included a public hearing on rezoning requests for three undeveloped Candelas parcels from commercial/industrial PUD to residential and commercial designations.
